scenario_prompt: Write the architecture section of a solution proposal, telling the migration as a narrative from the buyer's current estate to the target platform rather than as a list of components. Context: the current estate is Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines); the target is Google Cloud, using Google Compute Engine for compute, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the migrated data layer, and VPC Service Controls for the new project's governance perimeter. Return only the architecture narrative text.

## Architecture

The estate today runs 28 Microsoft SQL Server instances across 620 virtual machines on Hyper-V — a single hypervisor layer carrying both compute and data as one undifferentiated pool. Every workload, whatever its actual resource profile, is provisioned and patched through that same virtualization boundary, and every database sits inside a general-purpose VM rather than a managed service built for it.

The proposed target separates those two concerns. Compute moves to Google Compute Engine, so each of the 620 virtual machines is re-provisioned as a Compute Engine instance sized to its own workload rather than inherited from a shared Hyper-V host profile. The data layer moves separately: the 28 SQL Server instances migrate to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, replacing self-managed database VMs with a managed engine that takes over patching, backup, and failover as platform responsibility rather than estate-owned operational work.

[PF-1.17 GAP: no comparable, verifiable proof point for the SQL Server–to–PostgreSQL engine migration has been supplied — attach a named prior migration or benchmark before this ships]

Governance is established at the perimeter rather than inside each workload. VPC Service Controls defines a service perimeter around the new Google Cloud project, so the boundary that decides what can reach the migrated data layer is enforced once, at the project's edge, instead of instance by instance as it is today under Hyper-V.
